title: Potency narrows as cells specialise
caption: Following one line of descent from the zygote to a red blood cell, each cell can make fewer kinds of cell than the one before. Bone marrow transplants use the multipotent haematopoietic stem cells; induced pluripotent stem cells are adult cells turned back to the pluripotent stage.
alt: Five boxes in order: zygote (totipotent), inner cell mass (pluripotent), haematopoietic stem cell (multipotent), erythroid progenitor (unipotent) and red blood cell (specialised).
description: Zygote: totipotent, can make every cell type, and the placenta.
Inner cell mass: pluripotent, can make every body cell type, not the placenta.
Haematopoietic stem cell: multipotent, can make all the blood cells.
Erythroid progenitor: unipotent, can make red blood cells only.
Red blood cell: specialised, with no nucleus: cannot divide.
